features.title: #[serde(...)] helper attributes of the serde derives
features.notes: Probe evidence: tools/lust-port/tests/features/attrs_serde.rs is a lust-only oracle and lust rejects it (L0402). The attribute only has meaning under derive(Serialize) or derive(Deserialize), which map to ext.serde (a named gap, w-tail), so accepting and ignoring the helper attribute would change program behavior. It stays a clean reject, and this row stays separate so the helper-attribute count remains visible.

features.title: Adapter crate rustix 1.1.5: fs, process, termios, pipe, event, stdio subsets
features.notes: Lust adapter in library/deps (docs/ARCH.md 3.6), matched to the resolved package version; gate scripts/test-adapters.sh rustix (3 cases match the real crate; verified locally, the boat snapshot lacks the windows-link crate file cargo metadata needs). RawDir and std OwnedFd interop are absent, as the adapter README lists. Split from cinterop.system. See dependencies.json.

features.title: External crate serde 1.0.228 with derive feature: Deserialize/Serialize derives (proc macros)
features.notes: Named gap (w-tail). Split from ext.unknown_crate and derives.unknown. In ts-rust, serde is used only by the two codegen tools (tools/ts_ast_codegen, tools/ts_diagnostics_codegen): 15 derive(Deserialize) types fed by serde_json::from_str, with #[serde(default)], rename, rename_all = "camelCase", and untagged. The derive output is used, so the derives cannot be ignored. A lust adapter cannot stand in for a proc-macro derive: support needs a compiler built-in derive plus the serde trait framework, which is large. The tools run under Cargo (scripts/verify.sh: cargo run -p ts_ast_codegen) and their output files are committed, so the dev path does not need lust to build them. See dependencies.json (decision cargo-built-tool). Probes: ext_serde.rs (lust-only oracle; the derive is a clean reject, never a silent accept).

features.title: extern blocks and extern fn ABI
features.milestone_label: milestone 7: Threads and panics (sync, atomics, mpsc, panic recovery, C shims)
features.notes: Split from cinterop.system (w-cinterop). Probe: cinterop_extern.rs (the old cinterop_system.rs): a foreign fn call needs unsafe (unsafe.blocks) plus the extern surface; lust rejects both today (L0810, L0404).

features.title: External crate serde_json 1.0.150: from_str into Deserialize types
features.notes: Named gap (w-tail). Split from ext.unknown_crate. In ts-rust, serde_json::from_str is called 5 times in the two codegen tools, always into a serde Deserialize type (or a String), and its Error reaches output through Display. A correct adapter must match serde_json error text and positions byte for byte and needs ext.serde first, so it is large. The tools run under Cargo and their output files are committed. See dependencies.json (decision cargo-built-tool). Probes: ext_serde_json.rs (lust-only oracle).

features.title: unsafe blocks and unsafe fns
features.milestone_label: milestone 7: Threads and panics (sync, atomics, mpsc, panic recovery, C shims)
features.notes: Probe evidence: tools/lust-port/tests/features/unsafe_blocks.rs fails (L0404). PLAN.md keeps unsafe opt-in for C shims. Split from cinterop.system so plain unsafe use does not count as a system crate.

features.title: Attribute names lust rejects
features.milestone_label: milestone 4: The Rust core (modules, cfg, const/static, tuples, arrays, slices, Box, Result, Drop, std basics, macro_rules!)
features.notes: Probe evidence: tools/lust-port/tests/features/attrs_unsupported.rs fails (L0402). The attr.* catch-all lives here, after the accepted names in attrs.cfg and the serde names in attrs.serde, so a new attribute name blocks a file until lust knows it.

features.title: System crates (rustix, nix, signal-hook, jemalloc, zlib, local time)
features.milestone_label: milestone 7: Threads and panics (sync, atomics, mpsc, panic recovery, C shims)
features.notes: Cached rustc-built C ABI shims in milestone 7. See dependencies.json for the per-crate decision. Split by w-cinterop: raw pointer types are cinterop.raw_ptr, extern blocks are cinterop.extern, and #[global_allocator] is cinterop.global_allocator. No probe: each crate needs its own adapter probe.

features.title: Fn pointer types with lifetimes in fields, aliases, or nested types
features.milestone_label: milestone 6: Lifetimes ('static and '_ first, then lifetime params on user types)
features.notes: Probe evidence: tools/lust-port/tests/features/closures_fn_ptr_lifetime_field.rs fails (L0203): fn(&'a str) -> &'a str in a struct field. Also two named lifetimes in one fn pointer type, a named one inside a nested fn pointer or dyn type, and 'static Adt args there (type.fn_ptr.lifetime.complex). Split from closures.fn_ptr_lifetime (W-BORROW3).

features.title: Derives other than the lust set
features.notes: May be proc-macro derives from other crates. Proc macros stay out of PLAN.md. w-tail: every ts-rust use of this row was serde's derive(Deserialize), now ext.serde; this row stays as the catch-all for any other unknown derive.

features.title: Adapter crate tikv-jemalloc-ctl 0.7.0: Name/Access arena keys, epoch, version
features.notes: Lust adapter in library/deps (docs/ARCH.md 3.6), matched to the resolved package version; gate scripts/test-adapters.sh tikv-jemalloc-ctl (2 cases match the real crate). One-arena model: opt.narenas reads 1 and thread.arena 0, so a program that prints those values can differ from a jemalloc build (adapter README lists every such output); ts-rust only reads an arena and writes it back. Stats keys answer ENOENT and typed modules beyond epoch/version are absent. Split from cinterop.system. See dependencies.json.

features.title: External crate with no adapter decision yet
features.notes: Add a decision in dependencies.json and a rule here. Only crates in the scanner EXT list produce ext.* keys; other crates show in the dependency report as unknown. w-tail split out ext.serde and ext.serde_json (the ts-rust codegen tools); bare one-segment paths are locals, not crate roots (analyze.rs resolve), so this row has no ts-rust files left. It stays as the catch-all for the next crate.

features.title: Explicit for<'a> binders that elision cannot express

features.notes: Probe evidence: tools/lust-port/tests/features/lifetimes_hrtb_general.rs fails (L0203): one binder lifetime on two inputs. Also higher-ranked where clauses on types (for<'a> &'a T: IntoIterator). Split from lifetimes.hrtb (W-BORROW3).
